Definition: from G1 (as a negative particle) and G1062; unmarried:--unmarried.
BiblicalUsage: Agamos is 'unmarried' — and Paul uses it in his careful teaching on marriage in 1 Corinthians 7. He says it is good for the unmarried and widows to remain as he is, speaks of the unmarried woman's freedom to care for the things of the Lord, and contrasts the married person's divided attention with the unmarried person's single focus. The word is never a judgment; it is a state with its own freedom and its own calling.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe this word honours a state the world often pities. Paul does not treat the unmarried as incomplete — he treats singleness as a gift with room for undivided devotion, and marriage as a gift with its own duties, and both as callings from the same Lord.
